# Job Chapter 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 430r–430v

---

**37:1** At this also my-heart [libbi] trembles [yecherad] and-leaps [ve-yittar] from-its-place [mi-meqomo]. **37:2** Hear [shim'u], hear [shamo'a] the-raging [rogez] of-his-voice [qolo] and-the-rumbling [hegeh] from-his-mouth [mi-pihu] that-goes-out [yetse].

**37:3** Under all the-heavens [ha-shamayim] he-lets-it-loose [yishrehu], and-his-lightning [ve-oro] [reaches] to the-wings [kanfot] of-the-earth [ha-arets]. **37:4** After-it a-voice [qol] roars [yish'ag]; he-thunders [yar'em] with-the-voice of-his-majesty [be-qol ge'ono], and-he-does-not restrain-them [lo ye'aqvem] when his-voice [qolo] is-heard [yishame'a].

**37:5** God [El] thunders [yar'em] with-his-voice [be-qolo] wondrously [nifla'ot]; doing [oseh] great-things [gedolot] and-we-do-not know [ve-lo neda]. **37:6** For to-the-snow [la-sheleg] he-says [yomar], "Fall [hevei] [on the] earth [arets];" and-to-the-shower of-rain [geshem matar] and-to-the-shower of-his-mighty rains [geshem mitrot uzzo].

**37:7** In-the-hand of-every-man [be-yad kol-adam] he-seals [yachtom], for-the-knowing [la-da'at] of-all men of-his-making [anshei ma'asehu]. **37:8** And-the-beast [chayyah] goes [tavo] into-its-lair [be-mo-arev], and-in-its-den [u-vi-me'onoteiha] it-dwells [tishkon].

**37:9** From-the-chamber [min-ha-cheder] comes the-storm [suphah], and-from-the-scattering-winds [u-mi-mezarim] the-cold [qarah]. **37:10** By-the-breath of-God [mi-nishmat-El] ice [qerach] is-given [yitten], and-the-breadth of-waters [rochav mayim] is-in-constraint [be-mutsaq].

**37:11** Also with-moisture [be-ri] he-loads [yatri'ach] the-cloud [av]; he-spreads [yafits] the-cloud of-his-light [anan oro]. **37:12** And-it turns-about [mithhappekhet] by-his-guidance [be-tachbulotav] round-and-round [mesibbot], to-do [le-fo'olam] all that-he-commands-them [yetsavvem] upon the-face of-the-world [tevel] [on the] earth [artsah]. **37:13** Whether for-a-rod [le-shevet], or-for his-land [le-artso], or-for covenant-faithfulness [le-chesed] he-causes-it-to-find [yamtsi'ehu].

**37:14** Give-ear [ha'azinah] to-this, Iyyov; stand-still [amod] and-consider [hitbonen] the-wonders of-God [nifle'ot El]. **37:15** Do-you-know [hateda] when-God [Eloah] sets [be-sim] upon-them [aleihem], and-causes-to-shine [ve-hofi'a] the-light [or] of-his-cloud [anano]? **37:16** Do-you-know [hateda] of-the-balancings [al-miflesei] of-the-cloud [av], the-wonders [mifle'ot] of-one-perfect [temim] in-knowledge [de'im]?

**37:17** You whose-garments [begadeikha] [are] hot [chammim] when-the-land [erets] is-hushed [be-hashqit] from-the-south [mi-darom]? **37:18** Can-you-spread-out [tarqi'a] with-him [immo] the-skies [li-shechakim], hard [chazaqim] as-a-molten mirror [ki-re'i mutsaq]?

**37:19** Teach-us [hodi'enu] what we-shall-say [nomar] to-him; we-cannot-set-in-order [lo na'arokh] because-of darkness [mi-pnei choshekh]. **37:20** Shall-it-be-told [ha-yesuppar] to-him that I-would-speak [adabber]? If a-man [ish] speaks [dibbber], surely he-will-be-swallowed-up [yebulla].

**37:21** And-now, they-do-not see [lo ra'u] the-light [or]; it-is-bright [bahir] in-the-skies [ba-shechakim], and-a-wind [ve-ruach] has-passed [avrah] and-cleared-them [vatecharrem]. **37:22** From-the-north [mi-tsafon] gold [zahav] comes [ye'eteh]; upon God [Eloah] [is] fearsome [nora] splendor [hod]. **37:23** The-Almighty [Shaddai] — we-cannot-find-him [lo metsa'nuhu]; great [saggi] in-power [koach] and-justice [u-mishpat], and-abundant [ve-rav] in-righteousness [tsedaqah] — he-does-not oppress [lo ye'anneh].

**37:24** Therefore men [anashim] fear-him [yere'uhu]; he-does-not regard [lo yir'eh] all the-wise of-heart [chakhmei-lev]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.7 — "In the hand of every man he seals":** Hebrew *be-yad kol-adam yachtom* — a mysterious image. When God sends snow and rain, human labor ceases — God "seals" the hand of every worker, forcing humanity to acknowledge its dependence. Nature's extremes are a reminder of human limitation.

**v.13 — "for a rod, or for his land, or for chesed":** The three purposes of weather — punishment (*shevet*), provision for the land (*artso*), or covenant-faithfulness (*chesed*). This trinitarian purpose shows weather is not random but intentional. The inclusion of *chesed* is remarkable: storms can be acts of love.

**v.22 — "from the north gold comes":** Hebrew *mi-tsafon zahav ye'eteh*. The "gold" may refer to golden splendor (the aurora?) or to the clearing of storm clouds. The north (*tsafon*) is associated in Canaanite mythology with the divine mountain. Elihu sees divine glory breaking through.

*— EMET*
